verdict.rationale: Temporal's own CLI ships an embedded development service (`temporal server start-dev`) that starts a complete local Temporal Service with Web UI for fast local feedback, separate from any production deployment. Namespaces add documented isolation. This is real environment isolation, not a dry-run. However, the evidence never explicitly frames it as a test sandbox that guarantees no production data is touched, and no testing-specific environment is documented. missing for 10: explicit docs on isolating test runs from production data, a dedicated test/sandbox environment or testing framework, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: run an embedded development service when you need fast local feedback
This starts a complete Temporal Service with Web UI on your local machine.
Namespaces: Create and manage Namespace isolation, retention, and related configuration.
